To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we propose a novel method for reacquiring and tracking vehicles in video sequences, (2) we show that our method is effective for reacquiring vehicles in video sequences and (3) we show that the method can be extended to track multiple vehicles in a video sequence.

(i) we propose a new method for matching vehicle observations that are separated in time, and (ii) we show that our method outperforms state-of-the-art approaches for vehicle matching in terms of accuracy, robustness to change in appearance, pose and aspect.

we have developed a novel method that can match vehicles from non-adjacent frames in a video sequence, even in the presence of changes in pose and appearance.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the vehicle fingerprinting approach is effective in matching vehicles across multiple observations, thus enabling reacquisition of vehicles in a video stream and tracking across multiple video streams.
the proposed method is robust to significant changes in pose, aspect ratio and appearance of a vehicle across multiple observations and is suitable for re-acquisition of vehicles in videos.
the vehicle fingerprinting approach provides a general framework for matching vehicles across multiple time intervals.
